title.text: pandas II: cleaning the mess, with a log and a reconciled total

objects.text: How do we make a raw export trustworthy, and prove what we changed?

AI and Data Science Professional  |  Session 8 of 24  |  Module B: Python for data
KLAi Professional Learning  |  Jotham Martin Wambi

slides.notes:
Welcome back. Last session we opened a tidy file and asked it questions. Today the file is the kind that arrives in daily life: an export straight from a till system, with copies of the same line, two date formats, prices stored as text and spellings that wander.

We will clean it one defect at a time, keep a log of every change, and prove that the total is right. Today you also produce Project milestone 1, which you keep and show me for feedback.

slides.notes:
Here is what you can do by the end of today. You can remove duplicates, convert data types and dates, and clean text, with a rule you can state for every step. You can handle missing values by dropping, imputing or flagging, and you can check outliers with the interquartile range rule before you remove anything.

And you can write a data cleaning log and reconcile your cleaned total to a control total, then explain the reconciliation difference. Today is also Project milestone 1: a cleaned file with its log, which you show me for feedback and nobody scores.

title.text:
Your two hours: concepts first,
then the Project milestone 1 lab

objects.path: /sessions/focused-youthful-einstein/mnt/IUEA-Teaching-Resources/Professional_AI_Training/Business_AI/AI and Data Science Professional/05 Course Maintenance/KLAi Build/figures/x_plan_11.90x2.95_83d54561.png
objects.alt: The two hours in parts, in minutes

objects.text: Ideas with pictures first. Then you clean the file in the notebook. Then the checks and what you keep.

slides.notes:
We have two hours. The first ten minutes bring back Session 7 and set the question for today. Then forty-five minutes of concepts, with laptops closed: the eight defects in the file, the fix for each, and how we prove the total. After a ten minute break we open the notebook for a forty-five minute lab.

You clean the raw export step by step, keep a log, and reconcile the total. The last ten minutes are the exit check and what you keep. Today the lab produces Project milestone 1, so please protect that time.

title.text: Three questions from last time

runs.text: 1.  Which line counts the empty cells in each column of a DataFrame?
2.  How do you filter rows on two conditions?
3.  You report a figure from a filtered table. What goes beside it?

objects.path: /sessions/focused-youthful-einstein/mnt/IUEA-Teaching-Resources/Professional_AI_Training/Business_AI/AI and Data Science Professional/05 Course Maintenance/KLAi Build/figures/icon_question_2.80.png

objects.text: Answer aloud first. Then we check together.

slides.notes:
Three quick questions from Session 7. Answer aloud first, and then we check together. It is a warm-up to bring last time back.

Question one. Which line counts the empty cells in each column of a DataFrame?

A good answer is this. orders.isna().sum(): isna marks each empty cell True, and sum adds the Trues for each column.

Question two. How do you filter rows on two conditions?

A good answer is this. Put each test in round brackets and join them with & for and, or | for or.

Question three. You report a figure from a filtered table. What goes beside it?

A good answer is this. The row count, so the reader knows how many rows the figure covers.

If you missed one, check your notes from last session tonight. Now to today.

title.text: Answers to the three questions from Session 7

rows.text: Which line counts the empty cells in each column of a DataFrame?

You report a figure from a filtered table. What goes beside it?

objects.path: /sessions/focused-youthful-einstein/mnt/IUEA-Teaching-Resources/Professional_AI_Training/Business_AI/AI and Data Science Professional/05 Course Maintenance/KLAi Build/figures/icon_question_0.50.png

Here are the answers to the three warm-up questions. The line that counts the empty cells is isna followed by sum: isna marks each empty cell as True, and sum adds the Trues for each column. To filter on two conditions, put each test in round brackets and join them with the ampersand for and, or the vertical bar for or.

And a figure from a filtered table always needs its row count beside it. Today that habit grows into the data cleaning log, where we write the row count before and after every change. Which of the three did you find hardest?

title.text: Words we use today

rows.text: A table of every change to the data, with the row counts before and after and the reason. It is the audit trail of the cleaning.
Filling a missing value with a stated value, such as the median or a constant. Keep a flag to show which values were filled.
A value far from the rest. The IQR rule flags values more than 1.5 times the interquartile range beyond the quartiles.
A total that comes from a trusted source, such as the till system, used to test your own total.
The gap between your cleaned total and the control total. Explain it, or find the defect behind it.

slides.notes:
Five words for today. I give the plain meaning of each, and we use every one of them before the end of the session.

Data cleaning log. A table of every change to the data, with the row counts before and after and the reason. It is the audit trail of the cleaning.

Imputation. Filling a missing value with a stated value, such as the median or a constant. Keep a flag to show which values were filled.

Outlier (IQR rule). A value far from the rest. The IQR rule flags values more than 1.5 times the interquartile range beyond the quartiles.

Control total. A total that comes from a trusted source, such as the till system, used to test your own total.

Reconciliation difference. The gap between your cleaned total and the control total. Explain it, or find the defect behind it.

title.text:
Cleaning is a workflow: keep the raw file, fix
one defect at a time, log it, then reconcile

objects.path: /sessions/focused-youthful-einstein/mnt/IUEA-Teaching-Resources/Professional_AI_Training/Business_AI/AI and Data Science Professional/05 Course Maintenance/KLAi Build/figures/x_flow_11.90x3.90_9c3e4a3f.png
objects.alt: Cleaning is a workflow: keep the raw file, fix one defect at a time, log it, then reconcile

objects.text: Data cleaning means making a file correct and consistent enough to analyse. Each change is small, checked and written down.

slides.notes:
Cleaning is a workflow, and the workflow is the same on every file. First, keep the raw file exactly as it arrived, and never edit it. Second, make a copy, which we call df, and clean the copy. Third, fix one defect at a time, and check the row count after each fix.

Fourth, write each change in a log, with the rows before, the rows after and the reason. Fifth, reconcile: compare your total with a total that comes from a trusted source. Why do you think we change only one thing at a time?

title.text:
Eight defects are hidden in the
41,259 lines of the raw export

rows.text: What you see in the raw file

objects.text: Counts are for the raw file. After the 80 duplicates are dropped: slash dates 12,383, text prices 10,328, blank customers 10,626, negative quantities 1,179.

slides.notes:
The raw export has 41,259 lines, and eight defects. Eighty lines are exact copies of other lines. Dates come in two formats, and prices are sometimes text with the letters UGX in front. The same payment method is spelled 11 ways, and the branches 26 ways. Customers are blank in three different spellings.

Twelve lines have no quantity. And some quantities are negative, which are returns. The counts in the table are for the raw file. Later slides use the counts after the duplicates are dropped, which are a little smaller. Each defect has a fix, and today we do all eight in order.

Which of them would you spot first in Excel?

title.text:
read_csv turns N/A and NULL into NaN,
so three blank spellings are already one

objects.path: /sessions/focused-youthful-einstein/mnt/IUEA-Teaching-Resources/Professional_AI_Training/Business_AI/AI and Data Science Professional/05 Course Maintenance/KLAi Build/figures/x_ds_console_11.90x4.25_1fe9bbfd.png
objects.alt: read_csv turns N/A and NULL into NaN, so three blank spellings are already one

objects.text: The 1,833 walk-in labels stay as text. value_counts(dropna=False) counts the NaN too.

slides.notes:
A useful surprise. When I read the file as plain text, the customer column holds 5,051 empty cells, 3,113 cells that say N slash A, 2,483 that say NULL, and 1,833 that say walk-in. Four spellings of the same idea. But the normal read csv already treats empty, N slash A and NULL as missing, and turns them into NaN.

So pandas counts 10,647 missing values, the sum of the three. Only the label walk-in stays as text. That is helpful, and you should know it happens. Adding dropna equals False to value counts makes it count the blanks as well. What would you check if a column should never be blank?

title.text:
An exact duplicate repeats another record in
every variable, and drop_duplicates keeps the first

objects.path: /sessions/focused-youthful-einstein/mnt/IUEA-Teaching-Resources/Professional_AI_Training/Business_AI/AI and Data Science Professional/05 Course Maintenance/KLAi Build/figures/x_ds_before_after_11.90x4.25_afc0e1b5.png
objects.alt: An exact duplicate repeats another record in every variable, and drop_duplicates keeps the first

objects.text: Excel: Data, Remove Duplicates. pandas: duplicated(subset=...) checks chosen variables only.

slides.notes:
The first defect is the duplicate. A duplicate is a record that repeats another record in every variable. Look at the four real lines on the left. The two pairs are exact copies. The method drop duplicates keeps the first of each and drops the rest, so 80 lines disappear and 41,179 remain.

Then we test the key. Each line has a line id, the primary key, so after cleaning it should be unique, and the test returns True. That proves no line id repeats, which exact duplicates would break. It does not find two different lines for the same sale: duplicated with the subset setting checks repeats on chosen variables only.

In Excel the same tool is Remove Duplicates. Why is a unique key a good proof that the duplicates are gone?

title.text:
to_numeric converts text to numbers, and
errors decides what happens to a bad value

objects.text: errors raise (the default)

runs.text: Stops at the first bad value and names it.

objects.text: errors coerce

runs.text: Turns each bad value into NaN and carries on.

objects.text: Remove the text first, convert, then count the NaN.

slides.notes:
Next, data type conversion. The prices are stored as text, so they cannot be added. The function to numeric converts text to numbers, and its errors setting decides what happens to a bad value. By default it raises an error and stops, and the message names the first value it could not read: UGX seven thousand eight hundred.

That is the safe behaviour. With errors set to coerce, every bad value silently becomes NaN. On our raw prices that would blank 10,328 prices without a word. So remove the letters and the comma first, then convert, and always count the NaN afterwards. What would that count have told you here?

title.text:
Strip the letters and the comma, then
to_numeric: object becomes int64

objects.path: /sessions/focused-youthful-einstein/mnt/IUEA-Teaching-Resources/Professional_AI_Training/Business_AI/AI and Data Science Professional/05 Course Maintenance/KLAi Build/figures/x_ds_before_after_11.90x4.25_b7c4ffb2.png
objects.alt: Strip the letters and the comma, then to_numeric: object becomes int64

objects.text: A price stored as text cannot be added up. A number can.

slides.notes:
Here is the fix. The str dot replace method removes the letters UGX, and a second call removes the comma. The cleaned text goes into to numeric. Look at the real line on the left: UGX seven thousand eight hundred becomes the number 7800. 10,328 prices had that text.

The data type of the column changes from object, which means text, to int64, a whole number, and now it can be added. Notice the habit: we check the type and count the NaN straight after the conversion. Where else might a number hide as text in your own files?

title.text:
to_datetime with a format reads each date
style on its own, then fillna joins the two

objects.path: /sessions/focused-youthful-einstein/mnt/IUEA-Teaching-Resources/Professional_AI_Training/Business_AI/AI and Data Science Professional/05 Course Maintenance/KLAi Build/figures/x_ds_console_11.90x4.25_140ded9c.png
objects.alt: to_datetime with a format reads each date style on its own, then fillna joins the two

objects.text: %Y is the year, %m the month, %d the day. NaT means not a time: a date that failed.

slides.notes:
Dates come in two formats, so we read the column twice. The first read uses year, month, day and the second uses day, month, year, and each read turns what does not fit into NaT, which means not a time. The first read fails on 12,383 dates, the slash ones, and the second fails on 28,796, the dash ones.

The method fillna takes the first reading and fills the gaps from the second. After that no date is missing, and the earliest is 2024-01-01 and the latest 2025-12-28, which matches the two years of the file. Always check the range after a date conversion. Why does the range prove something?

title.text:
Reading day/month dates the wrong way
round raises no error, so learn the rule first

objects.path: /sessions/focused-youthful-einstein/mnt/IUEA-Teaching-Resources/Professional_AI_Training/Business_AI/AI and Data Science Professional/05 Course Maintenance/KLAi Build/figures/x_ds_date_fork_11.90x4.25_c972383e.png
objects.alt: Reading day/month dates the wrong way round raises no error, so learn the rule first

objects.text: Ask the data owner which date style the file uses, and write it in the log.

slides.notes:
This is the dangerous one. The text zero four slash zero nine slash twenty twenty five is a valid date both ways. Our rule says day first, so it is the fourth of September. If you guess month first, pandas reads it as the ninth of April and says nothing.

Of the 12,383 slash dates, 4,600 would silently get the wrong month, 7,388 would fail because the day is above twelve, and only 395 would be right by luck. The only defence is to learn the rule from whoever made the file, and to check the range afterwards.

Who owns the data in your workplace?

title.text: String methods fix text one rule at a time

rows.text: MM becomes mobile money, Entebe becomes Entebbe
Capital letter on the first word

objects.path: /sessions/focused-youthful-einstein/mnt/IUEA-Teaching-Resources/Professional_AI_Training/Business_AI/AI and Data Science Professional/05 Course Maintenance/KLAi Build/figures/icon_tag_0.34.png
/sessions/focused-youthful-einstein/mnt/IUEA-Teaching-Resources/Professional_AI_Training/Business_AI/AI and Data Science Professional/05 Course Maintenance/KLAi Build/figures/icon_tag_0.34.png
/sessions/focused-youthful-einstein/mnt/IUEA-Teaching-Resources/Professional_AI_Training/Business_AI/AI and Data Science Professional/05 Course Maintenance/KLAi Build/figures/icon_tag_0.50.png
/sessions/focused-youthful-einstein/mnt/IUEA-Teaching-Resources/Professional_AI_Training/Business_AI/AI and Data Science Professional/05 Course Maintenance/KLAi Build/figures/icon_tag_0.50.png
/sessions/focused-youthful-einstein/mnt/IUEA-Teaching-Resources/Professional_AI_Training/Business_AI/AI and Data Science Professional/05 Course Maintenance/KLAi Build/figures/icon_tag_0.50.png

objects.text: Excel twins: TRIM, LOWER, PROPER and SUBSTITUTE.

slides.notes:
Text defects are fixed with string methods, which you write after dot str. Strip removes stray spaces at the ends. Lower makes every letter lower case, so CASH and cash match. Title puts a capital letter on each word, so KAMPALA NTINDA becomes Kampala Ntinda. A dictionary with replace swaps listed values, such as MM to mobile money and the typo Entebe to Entebbe.

And capitalize fixes the first letter. In Excel the twins are TRIM, LOWER, PROPER and SUBSTITUTE. The order matters: strip and lower first, then replace, so the dictionary only needs one spelling of each. Why does the order matter?

title.text:
The same rules cut 11 payment spellings
to 3 and 26 branch spellings to 8

objects.path: /sessions/focused-youthful-einstein/mnt/IUEA-Teaching-Resources/Professional_AI_Training/Business_AI/AI and Data Science Professional/05 Course Maintenance/KLAi Build/figures/x_ds_console_11.90x4.25_dbdd4298.png
objects.alt: The same rules cut 11 payment spellings to 3 and 26 branch spellings to 8

objects.text: Check with value_counts that every remaining spelling is one you expect.

slides.notes:
Here are the rules applied. Branch gets strip and title, then a dictionary fixes the two typos. Payment gets strip and lower, then the dictionary changes MM to mobile money, and capitalize makes the first letter a capital. Before cleaning there were 11 payment spellings and 26 branch spellings.

After cleaning there are 3 payment methods and 8 branches, which is what the business has. A pivot table on the raw text would have split each real group into several. Always look at value counts afterwards to confirm. What would you do if a ninth branch appeared?

title.text:
A missing value has three
treatments: drop, impute or flag

objects.path: /sessions/focused-youthful-einstein/mnt/IUEA-Teaching-Resources/Professional_AI_Training/Business_AI/AI and Data Science Professional/05 Course Maintenance/KLAi Build/figures/x_icons_7.70x4.80_fe33bdcf.png
objects.alt: A missing value has three treatments: drop, impute or flag

objects.text: First ask what the blank means. Then choose, and write the rule in the log.

runs.text: Drop: a sale with no quantity (qty) cannot be priced.
Impute: a constant such as walk-in, or the median of a number.
Flag: keeps the memory that the value was missing.

slides.notes:
Missing values need a decision, and there are three treatments. Drop means remove the record, which is right when it is useless without the value, like a sale with a blank quantity, the qty variable. Impute means fill the blank with a stated value. For a number that is often the median, and for a label it can be a constant such as walk-in.

And flag means add an indicator variable, a column of True and False that says this value was missing. You can combine them: flag first, then impute. Whatever you choose, ask first what the blank means, and write the rule in your log. Which treatment would you use for a blank phone number?

title.text:
Flag first, then fill: 10,626 blank customers
become walk-in, and the flag remembers them

objects.path: /sessions/focused-youthful-einstein/mnt/IUEA-Teaching-Resources/Professional_AI_Training/Business_AI/AI and Data Science Professional/05 Course Maintenance/KLAi Build/figures/x_ds_console_11.90x4.25_edd039e2.png
objects.alt: Flag first, then fill: 10,626 blank customers become walk-in, and the flag remembers them

objects.text: The flag is an indicator variable: True where the value was missing before we filled it.

slides.notes:
Our customer blanks are walk-in shoppers, so we keep the records and fill the blank with the label walk-in. That is constant imputation. But first we add a flag, an indicator variable called customer missing, so we remember which blanks we filled. The print shows 10,626 flagged. After filling there are 12,456 walk-in lines, which is the flagged blanks plus the 1,830 lines that already said walk-in.

This is informative missingness from Session 2. Why is it better to flag before you fill than after?

title.text:
dropna with no settings would delete 26
percent of the lines, so name the column

objects.path: /sessions/focused-youthful-einstein/mnt/IUEA-Teaching-Resources/Professional_AI_Training/Business_AI/AI and Data Science Professional/05 Course Maintenance/KLAi Build/figures/x_ds_console_11.90x4.25_35bd2429.png
objects.alt: dropna with no settings would delete 26 percent of the lines, so name the column

objects.text: Run these before the customer step. Print the row count before and after every drop.

slides.notes:
A trap that runs without any error. You have blanks, you want a tidy table, so you call dropna with nothing in the brackets. It removes every line that has any empty cell. Because most walk-in lines have an empty customer, 10,638 lines disappear, which is 26 percent of the file, and every shilling they brought in goes with them.

Name the one variable that matters with the subset setting, and only the 12 lines with a blank quantity go. These counts come from the table before we filled the customers. Always print the row count before and after a drop. Which count would have warned you?

title.text:
Median imputation fills a blank number,
and an indicator variable keeps the memory

objects.path: /sessions/focused-youthful-einstein/mnt/IUEA-Teaching-Resources/Professional_AI_Training/Business_AI/AI and Data Science Professional/05 Course Maintenance/KLAi Build/figures/x_ds_before_after_11.90x4.25_a7631ab7.png
objects.alt: Median imputation fills a blank number, and an indicator variable keeps the memory

objects.text: The median resists extreme values. We do not impute quantities, which would change revenue.

slides.notes:
Imputation for a number. In the Nile Microfinance loans file, 379 of 8,000 loans have no monthly income. A standard treatment is median imputation: fill each blank with the median income, which is 642,600 shillings. We use the median because a few very high incomes would pull the mean upward.

And before filling we add an indicator variable, so a later model or a reader can tell the filled values from real ones. We do not impute the quantity in our orders, because an invented quantity would change the revenue we are trying to prove. When is a made-up value more harmful than a missing one?

title.text:
The IQR rule flags a value beyond 1.5
interquartile ranges from the quartiles

objects.path: /sessions/focused-youthful-einstein/mnt/IUEA-Teaching-Resources/Professional_AI_Training/Business_AI/AI and Data Science Professional/05 Course Maintenance/KLAi Build/figures/x_math_11.90x1.33_19aab063.png
objects.alt: The IQR rule flags a value beyond 1.5 interquartile ranges from the quartiles

rows.text: First quartile: 25 percent of the values are smaller.
Third quartile: 75 percent of the values are smaller.
Interquartile range: the spread of the middle half.
Values outside them are flagged as outliers.

objects.text: A negative lower fence means no value can be flagged on the low side.

slides.notes:
The standard way to flag an outlier is the interquartile range rule. The first quartile, Q one, is the value that 25 percent of the data lie below, and Q three is the value for 75 percent. Their difference is the interquartile range, the spread of the middle half.

For the order values in the orders file, Q one is 9,940 and Q three is 47,300, so the range is 37,360. The upper fence is Q three plus one and a half ranges, which is 103,340. The lower fence is negative, so nothing can be too small.

Any order above the upper fence is flagged. In pandas you get the quartiles with the quantile method. Why one and a half? It is the box plot convention of the statistician John Tukey.

title.text:
The IQR rule flags 2,100 of 30,229
orders, and each flag is a question to ask

objects.path: /sessions/focused-youthful-einstein/mnt/IUEA-Teaching-Resources/Professional_AI_Training/Business_AI/AI and Data Science Professional/05 Course Maintenance/KLAi Build/figures/x_ds_iqr_11.90x4.25_3ebe5544.png
objects.alt: The IQR rule flags 2,100 of 30,229 orders, and each flag is a question to ask

objects.text: Order values from orders.csv, the full file. The gold box is the middle half of the orders.

slides.notes:
Here is the rule drawn on the real order values. The gold box holds the middle half of the orders, from 9,940 to 47,300 shillings, with the median line at 23,200. The dashed fence sits at 103,340, and 2,100 orders lie above it. The axis is broken because the largest order, 3,104,000 shillings, is far to the right.

Being flagged does not mean being wrong. A flag is a question to ask about the record. Is it a real big purchase, a typing error, or a different kind of record?

objects.text: Returns are already inside the cleaned total as negative lines.

slides.notes:
This is the proof. The control total is the till system total for the same lines: 561,421,125 shillings. Our cleaned total is quantity times price, less the discount, summed over every cleaned line, and returns are inside it as negative amounts: 561,288,435. The difference is 132,690 shillings. We call it the reconciliation difference, and we must explain it.

The 12 dropped lines have a blank quantity, which is the likely cause. One unit of each would be worth 67,090 shillings, so the difference equals about 2.0 units per line, which is a normal quantity. This is an estimate, because the true quantities are not in the file.

We can name a likely cause, and we say so plainly. Could you explain a gap you had not traced?

slides.notes:
The reconciliation difference is the control total minus the cleaned total. A zero would be a perfect tie. A small difference with a named cause is acceptable. A difference that nobody can explain is a defect to hunt down. In our data the control total is 561,421,125, the cleaned total is 561,288,435, and the difference is 132,690 shillings.

Please use the name reconciliation difference. The word residual belongs to models, and we meet it in the regression sessions, where it means something different. Why is a tidy zero sometimes a warning sign?

title.text: Five likely mistakes in the lab and how to fix them

rows.text: Text is left in the price, so to_numeric cannot read it.
Remove UGX and the comma first, then convert.
Dates still missing after the fill
A format string does not match the text.
Match each format to its separator: dash or slash.
The column is already a number or a date.
Run each string method before the conversion.
Row count drops by about ten thousand
dropna was called with no settings.
Use dropna with subset set to the column qty.
Your net total is a little different
A step ran twice, or the returns were removed.
Restart and run all cells from the top. Keep the returns.
